title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Zambia: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Zambia: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Zambia: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: Planning medical coverage, incapacity safeguards, disability pension claims, and estate documentation during a serious or terminal illness in Zambia centers on National Health Insurance benefits, Powers of Attorney and formal wills, NAPSA or PSPF invalidity procedures, civil ID accuracy, and non-Apostille consular authentication. Because Zambia Revenue Authority (zra.org.zm) and Foreign Affairs (mofaic.gov.zm) portals present external TLS certificate validation issues and napsa.co.zm restricts automated external requests via firewall filtering, this guide cites live NHIMA, PSPF, DNRPC, Judiciary of Zambia, HCCH, and ZambiaLII sources.

steps.title: Health Insurance Benefits, Palliative Care, and Medical Records
steps.html:
• Confirm accredited inpatient ward, ICU, cancer/oncology, diagnostic imaging, physiotherapy, and essential medication coverage under the National Health Insurance Management Authority (NHIMA) Benefit Package [1][2].
  • Request certified specialist clinical summaries and permanent infirmity medical assessments from accredited hospitals, as Medical Board evaluations rely directly on original specialist clinical documentation [7].

steps.title: Powers of Attorney, Wills, and Estate Planning
steps.html:
• Execute a written Power of Attorney while legal capacity remains intact so a designated attorney-in-fact can handle banking, property, and High Court administrative matters overseen under the Judiciary of Zambia framework [5].
  • Draft and execute a valid written will satisfying the signature and witness requirements of the Wills and Administration of Testate Estates Act (Cap. 60), avoiding unintended statutory default distribution rules under the Intestate Succession Act (Cap. 59) or administration delays under the Administrator-General's Act [5][8].

steps.title: Invalidity Benefits and Beneficiary Nominations
steps.html:
• Private-sector contributors permanently incapacitated from regular employment can seek an Invalidity Benefit with the National Pension Scheme Authority (NAPSA) governed by the National Pension Scheme Act, 1996 and the National Pension Scheme (Medical Board) Regulations, 2016 (SI 95 of 2016) (contact regional NAPSA branches or member desks directly due to external firewall filtering) [6][7].
  • Public-service contributors can apply for Medical Retirement benefits through the Public Service Pensions Fund (PSPF) under the Public Service Pensions Act No. 73 of 2026 (lump-sum contribution refund plus Bank of Zambia interest for under 10 years of service, or monthly medical retirement pension at 10 or more years) and update ePSPF records and beneficiary designations [3][4].

steps.title: Civil Identity, Tax Records, and Title Preparation
steps.html:
• Ensure Green National Registration Cards (NRC), birth records, and passports held through the Department of National Registration, Passport and Citizenship (DNRPC) carry consistent spellings and identity numbers [9].
  • Compile ZRA Taxpayer Identification Number (TPIN) records, land title deeds, bank mandates, and the storage location of original executed wills.

steps.title: Cross-Border Document Authentication (Non-Apostille)
steps.html:
• Zambia is not a Contracting Party to the HCCH 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, so Apostille certificates do not replace embassy legalization [10].
  • Notarized powers of attorney, certified medical certificates, and civil status documents destined for foreign authorities require authentication through the Consular and Protocol Division of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation (Charter House, Lusaka) followed by legalization at the receiving state's mission [10].

contacts.name: National Health Insurance Management Authority (NHIMA)
contacts.note: Stand No. 27396, Alick Nkhata Road, Longacres, Lusaka (+260 211 356 498); oncology, inpatient, and essential medicine coverage.

contacts.name: Public Service Pensions Fund (PSPF)
contacts.note: Pensions House, Sapele Road, Lusaka; medical retirement claims and ePSPF member record updates under Act No. 73 of 2026.

contacts.name: National Pension Scheme Authority (NAPSA)
contacts.note: National Pension Scheme Act and SI 95 of 2016 Medical Board invalidity assessments (contact NAPSA offices directly due to external web firewall blocks).

contacts.name: Judiciary of Zambia
contacts.note: Plot 438 Independence Avenue, Lusaka; High Court registry and probate governance.
